runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

savePrompt.description: If true, the LLM prompt produced by the harness is included as a 'prompt' field on the action returned by core_harness, which causes it to be persisted in the episode replay. Defaults to false to keep replays small.

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

strictMode.description: If true, agents must return only {'submission': int} (no extra fields like 'thoughts'), and per-agent TIMEOUT/ERROR/INVALID counts as a loss for the offending agent only — other agents win. If false (default), any agent error halts and voids the entire episode, matching the lenient research-mode behavior.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

action.thoughts:
The current board state shows only two pieces placed so far, both in column 3: an 'x' at the bottom (row 5) and an 'o' directly above it (row 4). All other columns are empty, and it is player 'x's turn. No immediate win or forced block exists, as neither player has three connected pieces in any direction.

Placing in column 3 would drop an 'x' to row 3, creating the stack x-o-x (from bottom to top) in that column. This isolates the two 'x' pieces with an opposing 'o' in between, blocks any future vertical win in the center column, and fails to build any connected structure.

Instead, the optimal strategy is to connect to the existing 'x' at (row 5, column 3) by placing in an adjacent column. This creates an immediate horizontal pair at the bottom row. Columns 2 and 4 are symmetric and ideal for this, as they start a foundation for horizontal, vertical, or diagonal threats while staying near the center. Farther columns (0, 1, 5, 6) are less central and slower to develop into winning lines.

Column 4 is selected to begin building on the right side of the existing piece.

Final Answer: 4

action.thoughts:
The current board has empty columns except for columns 3 and 4, which each contain an 'x' at the bottom (row 5) and an 'o' directly above it (row 4). No player has three or more consecutive pieces in any direction, so there is no immediate win available. However, player 'x' can immediately create a double threat by extending the existing horizontal pair of 'x' pieces.

Playing in column 2 drops an 'x' to row 5, producing three consecutive 'x' pieces horizontally across columns 2-4 in the bottom row. This creates two separate winning threats on the next turn:
- Column 1 would complete four 'x' pieces across columns 1-4.
- Column 5 would complete four 'x' pieces across columns 2-5.

Player 'o' can respond with only a single move and thus can block at most one of those columns. On the subsequent turn, 'x' can play in the unblocked column to complete four-in-a-row horizontally and win. (The symmetric move in column 5 produces an identical double threat across columns 3-5, with winning extensions possible in columns 2 or 6.)

No other legal move creates an equivalent forcing win in two turns. Moves such as column 3 or 4 place an 'x' on top of the existing stack but produce neither three-in-a-row nor a double threat that 'o' cannot fully neutralize. Moves farther from the center (e.g., column 0 or 1) leave the existing 'x' pair isolated and allow 'o' to prevent any immediate threat.

Thus column 2 (or symmetrically column 5) is the optimal forcing move that guarantees a win with perfect play.

Final Answer: 2
